main_body: Timber-framed house: large hipped tile roof with a gabled cross-wing, half-timbered plaster walls, a door and a window, and a brick chimney
top_band: Roof slopes (orange/red tile with light highlight tiles), rows ~0-42 on the main mass: a tall, clearly visible top surface seen from above, ending at a dark eave line at row ~42; the front gable roof is also visible as slopes
evidence: Down a central column through the main body, the roof tile slopes run from row 0 to about 42 and end at a dark eave line with a shadow under it. Below that the plaster and timber wall runs from row 43 to about 73, with a dark timber frame, an inset door and a window. Roof slopes read as a large top surface, and the wall is a separate front face. The hip and gable slopes are shown and no receding isometric side face is drawn. This matches the reference houses.

style.evidence: The candidate is built in the same style as the Beodeul reference houses: tile roofs with per-tile highlights across about 5 tones, plaster speckle, timber with a dark brown outline, a brick chimney and a window with a flower box. The outlines are dark brown or red-brown tones, not near-black. The surfaces carry texture and are not flat fills, and the tile detail is as dense as the reference. It would sit next to the reference without looking thinner.
